published.title: Tech and Science, 24 July
published.html:
Tech and Science

INESC-ID joins artificial intelligence skills hub AISHA

Science Business

INESC-ID has joined AISHA, a Digital Europe Programme initiative building a pan-European AI skills hub focused on generative AI training.

Direct example of EU-funded AI skills infrastructure relevant to applied research institutions and workforce upskilling.

Should Horizon Europe take more note of vocational centres?

Science Business

Dutch MEP Brigitte van den Berg (Renew Europe) is pushing for Horizon Europe to give more weight to vocational training centres, backed by a June own-initiative motion.

Signals a possible shift in Horizon Europe priorities that could open funding routes for hogescholen and applied research.

Viewpoint: Europe’s AI problem is not merely competition, but control

Science Business

Three AI research leaders argue Europe's real AI problem is loss of control after the US ordered Anthropic to cut off Claude access for foreign nationals in June.

Frames EU AI sovereignty and dependency risks, relevant to governance debates he tracks.

Industry rejects move to cash contributions for EU Joint Undertakings

Science Business

The European Commission's proposal to require industry to make cash (rather than in-kind) contributions to Horizon Europe Joint Undertakings has met strong industry pushback.

A concrete funding-mechanism dispute that could affect how Horizon Europe partnerships are financed and structured.

Universities build policy expertise to meet growing role in funding

Science Business

The University of Lorraine has hired a six-person in-house EU policy team as universities increasingly build expertise to secure research funding tied to EU priorities.

A model of institutional adaptation to EU funding rules that Flemish hogescholen and universities may need to follow.

Google Hit With $1 Billion Fine By EU Over Search Engine Practices

NYT > Technology

The EU has fined Google €1 billion (reported as $1 billion) over anti-competitive search engine practices amid tense trans-Atlantic trade relations.

Shows the EU actively enforcing digital market regulation, relevant to his interest in tech governance and platform power.

published.title: Culture, 25 July
published.html:
Culture

Charli XCX’s A.G. Cook Tribute Song Is Great

Vulture

A closer look at the Charli XCX song on her new album devoted entirely to her longtime producer A.G. Cook.

Within a spare 11-track record, a two-and-a-half-minute tribute to a key collaborator stands out as its emotional core.

Charli XCX Successfully Delivers the Anti-Brat

Vulture

A review of Charli XCX's new album Music, Fashion, Film.

The claim on the table is that this record is the deliberate opposite of the brat persona that made her a cultural juggernaut.

One of the Greatest of Films, Visconti’s White Nights, Is Back in Theaters

Vulture

Luchino Visconti's 1957 film White Nights returns to theatres.

A critic makes the case for a film Visconti made while caught between being neorealism's founder and its supposed betrayer.

Voor de punk was er punk: “Er zaten al barsten in het optimisme van de sixties”

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

A history of what came before punk, tracing the cracks already in sixties optimism.

Nugget collector and Patti Smith Group guitarist Lenny Kaye argues punk bands were less an invention than a clean sweep of what already existed.

Overlooked No More: Barbara Rubin, Teenage Filmmaker at the Heart of New York’s Underground

NYT > Arts > Music

A profile of Barbara Rubin, teenage filmmaker of the New York underground.

She made the landmark film Christmas on Earth and brought together Warhol, Ginsberg and Dylan, yet has gone largely unrecognised until now.

Freddy Cannon, Rocker Who Sang ‘Palisades Park,’ Dies at 89

NYT > Arts > Music

An obituary for Freddy Cannon, the rock and roller behind Palisades Park.

Known as Boom Boom, he turned his mother's poem into the hit Tallahassee Lassie and helped define early rock and roll's teenage sound.

published.title: Culture, 24 July
published.html:
Culture

How Conor Oberst Survived Teenage Rock Stardom

NYT > Arts > Music

A long profile of Conor Oberst on three decades as a cult singer-songwriter, his personal struggles and writing political songs under Trump.

A substantial piece on a songwriter whose confessional, piano-adjacent tradition sits close to his taste.

Bonnie Tyler, zangeres van ‘Total Eclipse of the Heart’ op 75-jarige leeftijd overleden

Muziek - KnackFocus

Bonnie Tyler, singer of 'Total Eclipse of the Heart', has died at 75.

An obituary of a musician he would know from the pop canon.

Van Baby Rose tot Joey Alexander: de pop- en jazzalbums van de week

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

De Standaard's weekly pick of the best pop and jazz albums, including Baby Rose and pianist Joey Alexander.

A quick weekly scan for new jazz and piano releases in his wheelhouse.

Een mix van piano en Perzische percussie, en een van de beste Franse pianisten: de beste klassieke albums van het moment

De Standaard - Cultuur en media

De Standaard's roundup of the best current classical albums, featuring a piano-and-Persian-percussion project and a leading French pianist.

Piano-centred classical picks that fit his listening habits.

De film ‘Los Domingos’ getuigt van zeldzame intellectuele nieuwsgierigheid

Film - KnackFocus

A review of the Spanish film Los domingos, about a teenage girl choosing a religious life against her family's wishes.

An arthouse title praised for real intellectual curiosity, worth reading before deciding to see it.

‘The Odyssey’ is een zeldzaam beest van een blockbuster

Film - KnackFocus

A Dutch-language review of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, weighing its scale against its shortcomings.

A critical assessment of a major director's new blockbuster, for someone who follows serious cinema writing.
